title: Ciphers at War
description: Follow cryptography through the battlefields — from ancient military codes through the World Wars to Cold War espionage.

stops.label: Polybius Square
stops.note: Ancient Greek military signaling — fire-torch telegraphy across distances.

stops.label: Stager Cipher
stops.note: Union word-level route transposition, with code words and operational procedures.

stops.label: Confederate Vigenère
stops.note: Confederate repeating-key traffic and documented Union solutions, including delays and transmission errors.

stops.label: ADFGX
stops.note: WWI German field cipher — designed for Morse telegraph, broken by Painvin.

stops.label: ADFGVX
stops.note: The extended six-symbol system entered use in June 1918.

stops.label: Enigma
stops.note: Polish and Allied teams attacked particular Enigma models, settings and procedures; recovery was not universal.

stops.label: Lorenz SZ40/42
stops.note: Tiltman recovered key material in 1941; Tutte and colleagues inferred the machine structure by early 1942; Colossus later accelerated wheel-setting.

stops.label: Reading the Radio Log
stops.note: An invented two-day radio log: map a net and follow changing callsigns without decrypting a message.

stops.label: Nihilist Cipher
stops.note: A Russian revolutionary cipher combining Polybius coordinates with numerical addition.

stops.label: VIC Cipher
stops.note: A complex Soviet hand system combining a checkerboard and transpositions; the full historical key procedure exceeds this widget.
